old: It's named after something that grows from the very top of you.
Its Latin root literally means 'pertaining to the hair.'
Trace it back far enough and you land on caput — the word for 'head.'
clues: This adjective describes something extremely narrow. Surprisingly, its Latin ancestor meant pertaining to hair, and that word traces back even further to the word for head.
Scientists use it for tubes, cracks or vessels as fine as a single strand of hair, a narrowness far beyond merely thin or slender.
It names the body's tiniest blood vessels, linking arteries to veins, and the action that lets a paper towel wick up spilled water.
